s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss with intraocular hemorrhage and crystalline deposits
salient_findings: Glistening crystals in the anterior chamber
Iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous
key_facts: The patient is a young girl
The right eye is blind
Hyphema developed spontaneously
Vitreous hemorrhage occurred
Multiple glistening crystals were observed in the anterior chamber
The number of aqueous crystals increased as the hyphema resolved
Iridescent, needle-like crystals were seen floating in the aqueous
A morning glory optic disc anomaly was present
There was a low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina
Chronic retinal detachment was visualized after vitreous hemorrhage resolution

shortlist.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor

shortlist.label: Primary hyperoxaluria
shortlist.why_kept: Spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage with crystalline deposits

shortlist.label: Cystinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Crystalline deposits in the eye, consistent with cystine accumulation

shortlist.label: Morning glory syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Morning glory optic disc anomaly and low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina

shortlist.label: Chalcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intraocular hemorrhage and potential for copper deposition
